newsitem.title: ITALY: Deal signed to raise Venice theatre from the ashes.
newsitem.headline: Deal signed to raise Venice theatre from the ashes.

text.p: Venice's historic La Fenice (Phoenix) opera house, which was gutted by fire in January last year, will rise again in just over two years' time under a construction contract signed on Friday.

Italian building firm Impregilo, which won the 90 billion lire ($53 million) reconstruction contract, will work 18 hours a day from dawn to nearly midnight to complete the work in just 823 days by the September 27, 1999, deadline.
"Rebuilding deadlines will be respected," Venice Mayor Massimo Cacciari said at the signing ceremony. "I hope local residents will be tolerant but I believe it is a bearable sacrifice."
Reconstruction of the theatre was masterminded by internationally renowned Italian architect Gae Aulenti and will start early next month.
"Today we are starting afresh. In terms of structure and safety this Fenice will be a completely new theatre but it will be a very beautiful copy of the original," Cacciari said.
Impregilo won the contract after an international tender to restore the famous opera house which was ravaged by fire on January 29, 1996.
Two men who had been working on electrical refurbishment in the theatre were arrested earlier this year on arson charges.

Considered an architectural jewel, the theatre held priceless memories as the stage for premieres of some of Italy's most famous operas. It first opened in 1792 and was rebuilt once before, after a fire in 1836.
